post.caption: Balzac's cane had Paris talking for months. In 1834, Balzac ordered a cane topped with gold and turquoises. It cost 700 francs, and he bought it on credit. The knob hides a small capsule, and nobody knows what it held, and it holds pieces of a necklace Madame Hanska wore as a girl. Balzac wrote that this jewel threatens to become European, and gossip papers talked about the cane for about six months. In 1836, a short novel about the cane made its holder invisible. The cane is kept in the Maison de Balzac in Paris.
